newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO to bid for rest of Hungary's MHB.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO to bid for rest of Hungary's MHB.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Monday it would make an offer for the balance of Hungary's Magyar Hitel Bank (MHB) once its purchase of an 89.23 percent stake in the bank from the Hungarian state is finalised.
ABN AMRO said on Friday it would buy the controlling stake in the country's fifth biggest bank for $89.23 million and invest an extra $100 million over the next 12 months.

"We have committed ourselves, once the deal is finalised, to offer a pro-rata price for the remaining shares," ABN AMRO spokesman Tanno Massar told Reuters, adding he expected the purchase to be completed this calendar year.
He said the $100 million would be used to raise MHB's capital and upgrade its branch network, invest in information technology and train staff.
MHB, with 70 branches and about 2,500 staff, earned a net profit of 3.44 billion forints in the first eight months of 1996 from 1.4 billion for all of 1995.
The sale leaves the Hungarian state with a five percent stake, which it had planned to offer to management and staff.
The balance is held by the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and the World Bank's International Finance Corp.
